elements.element: Vendor must have a duty to defend.
elements.evidence: The clause states that “Vendor shall defend” against the specified claims.

elements.element: Vendor must have a duty to indemnify.
elements.evidence: The clause states that “Vendor shall defend and indemnify” and expressly covers resulting damages, costs, expenses, and reasonable attorneys’ fees.

elements.element: Customer and its Affiliates must be beneficiaries of Vendor’s defence and indemnity.
elements.evidence: The duties expressly run to “Customer and its Affiliates.”

elements.element: Vendor’s defence and indemnity must apply to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The clause applies to “any third-party claim.”

elements.element: Vendor’s defence and indemnity must cover allegations that the Services infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (a) covers allegations that the “Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.”

elements.element: Vendor’s defence and indemnity must cover allegations that the Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (a) expressly includes the Deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor’s defence and indemnity must cover claims arising from Vendor’s breach of law.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (b) covers “Vendor’s breach of Applicable Law.”

elements.element: Vendor’s defence and indemnity must cover a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (c) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor’s defence and indemnity must cover claims arising from Vendor’s gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (d) expressly covers Vendor’s gross negligence.

elements.element: Vendor’s defence and indemnity must cover claims arising from Vendor’s wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (d) expressly covers Vendor’s wilful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require notice of the claim.
elements.evidence: The indemnified Party must give the indemnifying Party “prompt written notice of the claim.”

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give the indemnifying party control of the defence.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the indemnifying Party “shall control the defence of the claim.”

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require reasonable cooperation from the indemnified party.
elements.evidence: The indemnified Party must “provide reasonable cooperation.”

elements.element: Customer’s indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Customer indemnifies Vendor for third-party claims arising from “content or materials provided by Customer for use in the Services.”

elements.element: Customer’s indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Customer’s breach of law.
elements.evidence: Customer indemnifies Vendor for third-party claims arising from “Customer’s breach of Applicable Law.”

elements.element: Customer’s indemnity must contain no triggers beyond Customer-provided content and Customer’s breach of law.
elements.evidence: The rendered Customer indemnity lists only Customer-provided content or materials and Customer’s breach of Applicable Law; no additional Customer indemnity trigger is included.

elements.element: Vendor must provide Customer an intellectual-property indemnity.
elements.evidence: Vendor indemnifies Customer for third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement arising from Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no exclusion for modifications made by Customer.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement arising from combinations with items not supplied or authorized by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no combinations exclusion.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement arising from compliance with Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no Customer-specifications exclusion.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must provide a remedy under which Vendor procures the right to continue using the affected item.
elements.evidence: No procure-right remedy appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must provide a remedy under which Vendor modifies the affected item to avoid infringement.
elements.evidence: No modification remedy appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must provide a remedy under which Vendor replaces the affected item with a non-infringing alternative.
elements.evidence: No replacement remedy appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must provide a refund remedy.
elements.evidence: No refund remedy appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to 3× annual fees.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no indemnity cap or 3× annual-fees super-cap.

result.reason: The operative addition fully implements the preferred position, including Vendor defence and indemnity, all required claim triggers, Affiliates, procedure, and the limited Customer indemnity. It does not implement the fallback’s exclusions, infringement remedies, or 3× annual-fees super-cap. The existing warranty-disclaimer language remains unchanged and consistent with the new indemnity. Drafting quality is poor as it fails to address settlement control/consent, prejudice from late notice, the effect of indemnitor's failure to defend, and whether indemnity is exclusive remedy, and the IP indemnity lacks standard exclusions and mitigation remedies.
